title: SPHEREx 2025-2026 spectra of 598 main-belt asteroids agree with AKARI 2.7 um band depths and show that a Gaia DR3 0.7 um band raises the 3 um band rate from 37% to 62% at all sizes from 16 to 400 km
abstract: Question: Can SPHEREx survey data measure the 2.7-3 um hydration band of main-belt asteroids, and how often does a Gaia DR3 0.7 um band come with a 3 um band? Vilchez et al. (2026) found in 20 asteroids that the 0.7 um band often occurs without the 3 um band, mainly below 100 km. Method: We matched 4,114 asteroids (H < 12.5) with Gaia DR3 reflectance spectra to 270,830 SPHEREx exposures (2025-04 to 2026-10), used JPL Horizons positions seen from SPHEREx, and did PSF photometry of 1,034 asteroids on 25,857 Level-2 files. The simultaneous D1 detector (0.75-1.1 um) normalises the D4 flux (2.4-3.8 um), which removes rotation and geometry. With a solar model, a NEATM thermal model and the Gaia reflectance at the D1 wavelength, we measured the band depth D2 at 2.70-2.88 um. Cuts and detection rules were set before the full photometry. Results: For 44 AKARI asteroids, D2 agrees with the AKARI 2.7 um depth (r = 0.93, slope 1.06, offset -0.026). Only 2 of 83 high-albedo controls pass the band rule. Among 501 low-albedo asteroids, 62% (164/266) with a Gaia 0.7 um band have a 3 um band, against 37% (87/235) without (Fisher p = 4e-8). The rate does not depend on size (61% below 100 km, 64% above; interaction p = 0.82). Only 6 of 102 objects with a 0.7 um band and no 3 um detection have a D2 limit below 5%, and 4 of them are at a > 3.2 au. Exploratory: the rate is 40% for 0.7 um depths of 1-2% (equal to no band) and 83% for depths of 3% or more; Ch types 95%; the rate falls outward in the belt. Limitations: the window favours sharp phyllosilicate bands and under-measures rounded 3.1 um bands; thermal-model choices change rates by up to 0.1; bootstrap errors are 2.2 times too small; SPHEREx quick-release calibration is preliminary. Rivkin 2012: use of the 0.7 um band as a proxy for the 3 um band.
